title: Delivery Projection
description: A seller's forward-looking projection of where one package's delivery will end up at the end of its flight, given the delivery reported so far. It is the numeric counterpart to the categorical `pacing_risk` indicator on `get_media_buys` and the forward counterpart to the backward-looking `pacing_index`. **Advisory only**: a projection is an advisory forecast, not a delivery record. It carries no contractual meaning on its own, and any commercial use of it is governed by the parties' terms. Reported actuals remain the delivery record, and `is_final` on the enclosing row does not make a projection final. This is the post-purchase counterpart to the pre-purchase `delivery-forecast.json`, which is a spend-to-delivery curve rather than a projection from actuals. Sellers that do not project omit the whole object; buyers MUST NOT read absence as 'on pace' or as any other state.

projected_impressions.description: Projected lifetime impressions for the package when its delivery ends (at the end of the flight, or earlier if the package reaches its goal or budget first). Lifetime means from the package's start, not from `reporting_period.start`: it is a cumulative total that includes delivery already reported, not the remaining delivery, and is not comparable to the row's period `impressions` unless the reporting period covers the flight to date. Fractional values are allowed; it is a forecast and is not rounded to match reported impressions. Omit when the package is not impression-denominated or the seller does not project impressions.

projected_spend.description: Projected lifetime spend for the package when its delivery ends, on the same lifetime basis as `projected_impressions`. Denominated in the package row's own `currency` (not the media-buy row currency) and, for `revenue_share`, computed the same way as the row's `spend`. Omit when the seller does not project spend.

projected_end_state.description: The package-level judgment of where delivery lands, measured against the package's binding constraint: whichever of its goal or budget the package would reach first. The two projected totals are supporting numbers and are not classified independently. `on_pace`: the package is projected to reach the binding constraint at flight end, within the seller's tolerance. `complete`: the package is projected to reach it before flight end, with the undelivered share of the flight below the seller's materiality threshold, so it simply finishes early. `early_exhaustion`: the package is projected to reach it before flight end, with the undelivered share of the flight at or above the materiality threshold. `underdelivery`: the package is projected to fall short of the binding constraint at flight end by more than the seller's tolerance. There is no over-delivery state: a package projected to exceed its constraint is projected to reach it early. Tolerance and materiality are the seller's own thresholds, which it SHOULD also use for the `pacing_risk` indicator when it emits that indicator. They are not exposed, so buyers SHOULD NOT compare end states across sellers as if the thresholds matched. `complete` is a projected early finish, unrelated to `delivery_status: completed`. Clients on an older schema version SHOULD tolerate an unrecognized value.

enumDescriptions.on_pace: Projected to reach the binding constraint (goal or budget) at flight end, within the seller's tolerance.
enumDescriptions.complete: Projected to reach the binding constraint before flight end, with the undelivered share of the flight below the seller's materiality threshold. A benign early finish.
enumDescriptions.underdelivery: Projected to fall short of the binding constraint at flight end by more than the seller's tolerance.
enumDescriptions.early_exhaustion: Projected to reach the binding constraint before flight end, with the undelivered share of the flight at or above the seller's materiality threshold.

basis.description: The class of method the seller used. Parameters of the method (window length, model name) go in `ext`. Clients on an older schema version SHOULD treat a value they do not recognize like `seller_defined`.

as_of.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the latest delivery data the projection was computed from. Independent of the row's `reporting_period` and may precede the response time because reporting lags. The projection MAY be recomputed when the row is superseded by a wider `measurement_window`; `is_final` on the row describes the actuals, not the projection. Buyers comparing two reads compare `as_of` first.
